subject.title: fix(memory-core): use longer backoff for 429 rate-limit embedding errors (#108893)

question: Should memory indexing wait through the proposed bounded 429 schedule of approximately 10s, 20s, 40s, 60s, and 60s before surfacing a rate-limit failure?
rationale: The patch is internally consistent and has after-fix evidence, but the maximum user-visible index latency is an intentional runtime policy tradeoff that source inspection cannot settle.

options.title: Accept the bounded recovery window
options.body: Merge the current policy so ordinary short-lived provider cooldowns can clear while transport failures retain their existing short schedule.

options.title: Choose a shorter policy
options.body: Ask for a reduced retry budget or a narrower condition if prompt failure is preferred to a multi-minute memory-index wait.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded recovery window
recommendation.body: Merge the current policy so ordinary short-lived provider cooldowns can clear while transport failures retain their existing short schedule.
